title: Generated record batches, second version: which integrity rule does the batch violate?
decision: which of the 6 to 9 listed integrity rules a batch of records breaks (in one place, by a near miss), or none

source.name: generator build/gen_record_rule.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: consistent background data (tax, totals, dates, dated references), status convention written in the state, none share asserted; second version (v2) of 2026-10-07, DIFFICULTY = "v1" regenerates the first version byte for byte

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
skill: check a batch of records against 6 to 9 integrity rules (keys and pairs that must not repeat, look-ups in reference lists with a status, limits that depend on another field, stored totals, running numbers, references between records) and name the one broken rule, or none
knobs: records per batch 10 / 16 / 24 (meta.level 1 / 2 / 3); 6 to 9 rules, 3 to 5 of them of the kinds that need a computation, two records or two lists; violations one step from valid; valid look-alikes of every listed rule; oddities that no listed rule covers
notes: gen_v4 (2026-10-08): outside the planted violation and the one or two deliberate oddities (meta.oddities) every record keeps the relations between its own fields (tax = round(net x tax_rate / 100), stored totals, second date not before the first) and a record that names an earlier record is dated after it (meta.background lists them); a state with a status column says what a status counts for; the share of none is asserted (0.120 / 0.120 / 0.120 at levels 1 / 2 / 3, about 1 / mean number of options). Version v2 (harder than the first version, which is regenerated byte for byte with DIFFICULTY = "v1"). 600 items = 150 batches x 4 (group): the same batch with four different answers - one planted violation each of three or four different rules, and in 72 batches the untouched batch (none; 0.12 of the items, about 1 / mean number of options). Options differ per item: one key per rule (R1 ... Rk, k = 6..9, option text = the sentence of the rule) plus none; options = the maximum (10), chance = the mean of 1 / number of options. Thirteen rule kinds (meta.deviation, 40 or 41 violating items each, 13 or 14 per level): the six of v1 (unique, reference, range, conditional, date_order, allowed) and composite (a pair of fields is unique), ref_active (key in a list AND with a status there), dep_range (limits depend on another field), xor (exactly one of two fields filled), derived (stored total = product or sum), sequence (a number rises by one from record to record), self_ref (names the key of an EARLIER record); every schema lists 3 to 5 of the seven new kinds. Violations are near misses (meta.variant); every batch holds a valid look-alike of every listed rule, and most hold oddities that no listed rule covers (meta.oddities), which are not violations. meta.level 1 / 2 / 3 = 10 / 16 / 24 records (200 items each); two layouts of the records (JSON lines, table) and two of the lists. The key of the violated rule and the position of the gold option are spread evenly per number of rules; a listed rule of any kind is the broken one equally often. State length 2535 to 10507 characters (median 4751). The truth is computed on the structured records (meta.spec); the script asserts that a violating item breaks exactly the gold rule in exactly one place and a none item nothing.
